parallel.requirements: Recognized the five verification layers plus the requirement that run.sh emit KEY: VALUE metrics and that each completed requirement produce a non-empty patch.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Delegated the five layer implementations to swarm children while retaining run.sh, git, patch, and final assembly responsibility in the parent.
parallel.implementation: Children reported completed z3, fixedpoint, spacer, and horn_translator modules; cex_minimizer children aborted, and the parent later worked directly on CEGAR code before cancellation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The completed child work was not adopted into the durable submitted tree: git log shows only the initial commit and the harness collected zero requirement patches.
parallel.verification: Child handoffs reported local checks, but official integrated verification ran the unchanged stub and failed all Z3 output tests.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Final run.sh and requirement patches were absent, cex_minimizer was not durably delivered, and the official output contained no required experiment metrics.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same five-layer Z3 verification stack and the run.sh/patch workflow obligations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used one serial owner to implement and commit requirements in sequence, without delegation or subagent activity.
serial.implementation: Committed implementations for z3, uz_fixedpoint, spacer, and horn_translator, with tests and module entry points; cex_minimizer was not committed.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Produced four non-empty requirement patches and wired run.sh progressively so the official harness executed multiple modules.
serial.verification: Official tests passed all Z3, fixedpoint, and Spacer checks, then failed Horn because expected metric names were missing from output.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run remained failing due Horn metric contract mismatch and lack of a completed cex_minimizer requirement patch.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run had the same five-layer verification task and the same run.sh plus per-requirement patch obligations, then delegated implementation work for all five layers.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had the same task contract and pursued the layer requirements directly, generating patch artifacts for four requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized the broad task, but serial converted more of the requirement contract into durable patches and executable output while parallel left the final contract unmet.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split the layers across five children and reserved cross-cutting run.sh/git assembly for the parent; one CEX child aborted and four children returned module-level work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked sequentially in one agent and produced commits for z3, uz_fixedpoint, spacer, and horn_translator.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel split generated component handoffs but left adoption with the parent, whereas serial kept implementation and commit ownership in one linear flow.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child briefs gave module-scoped contracts and explicitly prevented children from changing run.sh or committing, so their returned outputs needed parent integration.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent directly edited modules and the run.sh entry point as part of each requirement patch.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The key interface boundary was not missing technical API information; it was the parent-held delivery boundary between child modules and the final executable patch set.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child handoffs reported completed z3, fixedpoint, spacer, and horn modules, and the parent later worked directly on cex_minimizer before cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial committed concrete source and test changes for four layers, with the z3 patch adding solver code and run.sh invocation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel work existed mostly as child and late-session workspace changes; serial preserved its implementation path as committed requirement patches.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Completed child results were visible to the parent, but they were not converted into final patches or the final entry point before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial closed each implemented requirement with a commit and patch file, so intermediate work became durable before final evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The decisive lifecycle difference was missing adoption of retrievable parallel results versus serial commits after each requirement.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: No concrete overwrite or collision was needed to explain the failure; the final shared tree still showed only the initial workspace and zero requirement patches.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integration was visible in four requirement patches and progressive run.sh updates.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel failed at final shared-state adoption rather than conflicting writes, while serial integrated work into the submitted tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had child-level reported checks, but official integrated verification executed the stub and missed all Z3 metrics.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial official verification passed Z3, fixedpoint, and Spacer, then failed because Horn expected metric names were absent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial reached evaluator-aligned execution for three layers, while parallel never got past the first Z3 output contract because run.sh remained a stub.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent three timed-out rounds, including a late direct cex_minimizer takeover that produced metrics but was canceled before final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but only after four committed requirement patches and an executable run.sh reached the official tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted time, yet the serial run had already made substantial durable progress, whereas the parallel run closed before joining and committing delegated work.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official outcomes are failures. The material difference is coverage and delivery: parallel delegated implementation and received useful child results, but did not join them into commits, requirement patches, or run.sh, so official tests saw the initial stub. Serial delivered four committed requirement patches and reached many passing tests before failing on Horn metric names.
parallel_contributors: Completed child module implementations were visible but not adopted into the final submitted tree.
The final parallel run had zero requirement patches and the unchanged run.sh stub, so evaluator output lacked even Z3 metrics.
Late parent CEX work was canceled before commit, patch generation, or final run.sh integration.
serial_contributors: Serial committed z3, uz_fixedpoint, spacer, and horn_translator patches and updated run.sh for those layers.
Serial official tests therefore passed Z3, fixedpoint, and Spacer checks before failing on Horn metric expectations.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial horn_translator produced HORN_CLAUSES_GENERATED style metrics while the evaluator expected HORN_PROGRAMS_PARSED and related metric names.
Serial did not complete a cex_minimizer requirement patch, but the visible official failure stopped at Horn metrics.
evaluator_effects: status.json evaluation supplies solution_passed but not validator-recognized passed/total counts; detailed visible counts come from results.json and post-test artifacts.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: Supported comparative contributor to the coverage gap, not an exclusive root cause and not a discordant official pass/fail outcome.

candidates.reason: Implementation owners existed: five child tasks were explicitly assigned module implementation work.
The parent retained integration responsibility, so the problem is inactive adoption rather than no assigned integration owner.
The parent explicitly kept run.sh and git assembly work, so final assembly was owned even though it was not completed.
The parent/orchestrator owned the end-to-end pipeline; no separate ownerless pipeline boundary is proven.
No mandatory serial preflight blocked productive implementation; children began implementation work immediately.
The parallel run was not merely an investigation phase; it delegated implementation tasks from the start.
Deadline pressure existed, but the directly evidenced defect is unjoined completed implementation work, not capacity diverted from a separate critical path.
Fan-out and timeout are visible, but the retained join boundary more specifically explains the lost work and final stub.
The cex child was complex and aborted, but the main realized failure for passed-child work is missing adoption, and the parent later took over CEX work.
The child briefs supplied the module contracts and intentionally excluded run.sh because the parent reserved assembly; missing final delivery was not a hidden child requirement.
No incompatible separately produced interfaces or names are proven; the issue is that returned implementations were not joined.
The returned child handoffs preserve the important module outputs and caveats; no known finding disappeared through transfer.
The handoffs were long but structured and visible; there is no proof their size itself prevented the parent from using them.
No receiver acted on superseded handoff information; the final failure was omission of adoption.
No unadjudicated incompatible reports or contracts are visible between children.
The parent did not make a successful whole-task completion decision; the run timed out and the evaluator found the stub.
Later rounds had visible prior workspace and handoff state; repeated work was not caused by an absent checkpoint alone.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: One CEX child was interrupted, but the parent later resumed that scope directly; the retained consequence is missing join of completed work.
No complete directly promotable final package existed because cex and run.sh/patch assembly were still unfinished.
There is no evidence of a child result merged after integrated verification without a post-merge check.

Completed delegated implementations were returned to the parallel parent, but the parent did not adopt them into committed requirement patches or the final run.sh before closure; serial shows the corresponding join path through requirement commits and run.sh edits.
candidates.realized_consequence: The submitted parallel state retained the stub executable and zero requirement patches, causing official tests to observe no Z3 experiment output.
candidates.near_match_reason: No complete final package was directly ready to promote; the observed boundary is adoption of retrievable child implementations into the delivered tree.

candidates.reason: The missing artifact was implementation adoption, not a verifier result trapped below the parent.
The parent did take over cex_minimizer work in round 3 and obtained CEGAR metrics before cancellation.
Completed child results were not merely ignored at a decision point; the concrete failure was not joining implementations into the deliverable.
The parent inspected and acted on progress, including direct CEX work, so it was not simply waiting blindly for timeout.
No competing incompatible file-scope designs are proven.
No live same-file edit collision is visible.
No source replacement or deletion of another actor-owned module is proven.
No actor overwrote the executable deliverable owned by another actor.
